title: Refused service at a restaurant: his father and the color line
summary: A restaurant manager turned away Thompson and his light-skinned father; this started his thinking about racial strife.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Specific. Not only just a black boy but a light complected black boy, of a father who looked like a white man. My father did look like a white man, in fact he had more white look than anybody else. In fact it was during this time my father took me into a restaurant he'd been going in for several months, alone, and he took me into this restaurant one day, sat me down to eat, and the waiter came over and said, I'm sorry, the manager would like to see you.

And my father said, oh, yes okay. And the manager came over, and he asked me -- he asked my father, said what nationality are you. Well, my father being a very, very, very educated man and having plenty of experiences in dealing with people, I noticed -- and he mentioned before that he gave him a very simple answer. He said, I'm connected with the Negro race. At that time blacks were known as colored and Negro. And he said I'm connected with the Negro race.

And the guy said, I'm sorry, but we don't serve any Negroes in here. And this was because, even though my complexion was light, it was not white. And my hair was of the grade of black people. And my father went out naturally disgusted, and this is what started me off to thinking about not only economics but racial strifes of black people, which I think is very important. Or perhaps maybe you might not think it important.
I think it very important. I don't think there's anybody left today that doesn't, would you.

I want to be clear, as is become a famous saying now, I want to make it absolutely clear. But I want to give you as many facts as I can, and I think as I slowly go through this life of mine I think these things are important. And since this material is to be kept by officials who think it might be interesting and important, I think I should try to get in every aspect of my brain and my mind,
who is Sir. Charles Thompson. Right.
Who was born Charles Philip Walker Thompson.
How old were you when that happened, at the restaurant?
This was during the time, in this period -- I don't know exactly --
It was in this period, give or take before or after I was 12. But as I said it's like the center of my beginning, the age 12.
